summary: The @gyomu/schema package provides a comprehensive, type-safe framework for modeling domain entities, infrastructure services, and application metadata. It leverages Effect schemas to facilitate robust data validation, automated CRUD generation, and consistent error handling across the system. The package also includes advanced analysis capabilities for parsing and documenting TypeScript code structures.
responsibilities: Provide a centralized framework for defining and validating domain-specific business entities.
Automate the generation of CRUD schema suites from entity definitions.
Establish a consistent, trait-based error handling and diagnostic context strategy.
Offer utility structures for parsing and analyzing TypeScript code, symbols, and dependencies.
Maintain high-level abstractions for I/O, network operations, and AI-driven workflows.
Ensure type-safe data conversion and operational result consistency.

capabilities.name: Domain Entity Modeling
capabilities.description: Definition of business entities using structured schemas, supporting audit fields, UI annotations, and automatic generation of CRUD operations.

capabilities.name: Structured Error Handling
capabilities.description: A robust system for defining domain-specific errors with consistent context, behavioral traits, and operational policies for logging and retries.

capabilities.name: TypeScript Analysis Framework
capabilities.description: Foundational tools for static analysis of TypeScript code, including symbol mapping, dependency tracking, and JSDoc metadata extraction.

capabilities.name: Result and Validation Patterns
capabilities.description: Standardized result schemas and utility patterns for wrapping operations, ensuring predictable communication between layers.

capabilities.name: Operational Lifecycle Services
capabilities.description: Management of system lifecycles for I/O, network, and AI requests, including retry strategies, timeouts, and state tracking.

capabilities.name: Data Format Utilities
capabilities.description: Advanced conversion and normalization utilities for temporal types, JSON objects, and character encodings.

designDecisions: Utilizes Effect for all schema definitions and effectful operations to ensure strong type safety and predictable error composition.
Employs branded types and nominal branding to provide semantic clarity and prevent accidental type mismatches.
Decouples domain definitions from implementation, allowing for automated generation of schema suites (CRUD) without boilerplate.
Implements a trait-based approach to error handling to allow granular control over retryability and logging behaviors.
Utilizes a recursive schema approach for modeling complex or nested structures such as JSON and document segments.
usageGuidance: Use the `defineEntityCrudSchemas` utility when creating new business entities to ensure consistent select, insert, and update capabilities.
Always extend or wrap errors using the provided GyomuError context tools to maintain system-wide observability.
Leverage the provided Effect runners and logging wrappers when implementing business logic that interacts with external services.
Use branded types (e.g., UserId) for identifier properties to leverage TypeScript's type-checking and avoid domain-level data confusion.
Refer to the `typescript` analysis schemas if building tooling that requires programmatic introspection of source code.
